- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85% of recent high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline at 5–7% below peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–4% downward bias in next forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values if sentiment volatility > 0.5.
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative signals (e.g., 3+ consecutive -1.0), model underperforms; increase forecast by 2–5% to counteract pessimism.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) or mixed, model often misreads trend; use 2-day moving average of history to anchor forecast.
